findings.title: Shared CORS Vercel suffix rule is spoofable: an attacker-named Vercel project's production alias ends with '-settlement-forge.vercel.app'
findings.evidence: `if (url.protocol === 'https:' && url.hostname.endsWith(VERCEL_DEPLOY_SUFFIX)) return true;` — the comment asserts "The team scope is the trailing segment and is owned by us — an attacker cannot deploy under it", but Vercel production aliases are `<project>.vercel.app` in a global first-come namespace: project name `evil-settlement-forge` yields `evil-settlement-forge.vercel.app`, which passes the suffix check.
findings.why: The allowlist's fail-closed invariant (documented as spoof-proof) is falsifiable: a hostile origin gets an exact ACAO echo plus Allow-Credentials:true on every edge function. Practical impact is bounded (auth is bearer-token, not cookie), but the module's central security claim is wrong as written.
findings.fix_shape: Tighten to the deploy-URL shape the comment actually assumes: require the full `<project>-<hash>-settlement-forge.vercel.app` pattern (e.g. /^[a-z0-9-]+-[a-z0-9]{9}-settlement-forge\.vercel\.app$/) or enumerate via ALLOWED_ORIGINS; add a spoof-shaped negative case to cors.test.ts.
findings.deferral_checked: No round-1 entry (the Vercel rule postdates round 1); not in playbook §0.0.2 or any in-file deferral note — the comment claims safety rather than deferring it.

findings.title: Pre-parse body-byte caps are inconsistently applied: five anon-reachable functions buffer unbounded request bodies
findings.evidence: `const { product, checkoutToken, ... } = await req.json();` runs before the rate limiter and the MAX_DOSSIER_BYTES check (which re-serializes post-parse); auth-recovery:261, send-email:359, log-client-error:81 parse unbounded anon bodies; stripe-webhook:909 `await req.text()` buffers before signature rejection. ingest-events/generate-narrative/generate-chronicle all cap bytes pre-parse.
findings.why: The codebase established the byte-cap discipline (and fixed the UTF-16 variant with regression tests) but never swept it across the anon surface; a single oversized POST forces full buffering+parse per request, bounded only by platform limits.
findings.fix_shape: One _shared/readBodyCapped.ts helper (text + byte cap + parse) adopted by all five; caps per function (create-checkout ~600KB to fit the 512KB stash, others 64KB). Mirrors the existing generate-chronicle pattern.
findings.deferral_checked: Round-1 register: body caps flagged and fixed only for generate-narrative/chronicle/ingest-events; no recorded decision to exempt the rest. No in-file deferral notes at the parse sites.

findings.title: checkout.session.async_payment_failed is unhandled — a reserved redeem-code seat leaks permanently on a deferred payment that fails
findings.evidence: The switch handles completed/async_payment_succeeded/expired but `grep async_payment_failed` finds nothing in supabase/functions. Traced: a session that completes with payment_status='unpaid' defers fulfillment; if the async payment then fails, `expired` never fires for a completed session, so revert_redemption never runs.
findings.why: The bound reservation stays 'reserved' forever: that user's once-per-user row is burned and the code's uses_count stays consumed — deferred money leaked with no operator signal. Rare today (card-only checkout), but the redeem lifecycle claims closure.
findings.fix_shape: Add `case 'checkout.session.async_payment_failed':` calling revert_redemption(session.id) — identical body to the expired case; claim-once semantics make it race-safe with a later success.
findings.deferral_checked: No round-1 entry, no in-file seam note (the async_payment_succeeded comment discusses the success leg only); not in playbook ledgers.

findings.title: ingest-events actor first-touch races remain: concurrent device/user link inserts can mint divergent actor ids (round-1 backend-6, still open)
findings.evidence: `await admin.from('analytics_device_links').insert({ device_key: deviceKey, actor_id: actor });` — insert error unchecked, freshly-minted actor returned regardless; resolveUserActor's upsert with ignoreDuplicates:true (line 121) returns its own candidate even when a concurrent writer's row won.
findings.why: Two concurrent first-touch envelopes attribute events to an actor id that never became the durable link — a permanent funnel-stitching blemish in the analytics corpus, invisible at write time.
findings.fix_shape: Upsert with onConflict:'device_key' then re-select the winning actor_id (same for the identity link) — one round-trip more on the cold path only.
findings.deferral_checked: docs/COMPREHENSIVE_REVIEW_2026-07-13.md line 1387: [backend-6] LOW/probable — recorded, verified still present at HEAD; carried at the register's severity.

findings.title: ingest-events swallows insert failures into a 202 and drops event/edit/pulse overflow uncounted — asymmetric with the counted snapshot cap
findings.evidence: `const { error } = await admin.from('analytics_events').upsert(...); if (!error) accepted.events = ...` — on error the response is still 202 with no rejected entry and no log; `body.events.slice(0, 50)` (line 231), edits slice(0,20), pulseEffects slice(0,60) silently discard overflow while snapshots overflow is pushed to `rejected` as 'snapshot_cap_exceeded'.
findings.why: A DB-side failure or an over-batching client loses telemetry invisibly — the exact silent-loss class the SERVER_SNAPSHOT_CAP fix (lib-infra-3) was written to eliminate, still open on the other three planes.
findings.fix_shape: Log insert errors (logError) and count overflow rows into `rejected` with 'event_cap_exceeded'-style reasons, mirroring the snapshot treatment; optionally surface accepted<sent to the client queue for re-spill.
findings.deferral_checked: Round-1 fixed only the snapshot plane (lib-infra-3); no recorded decision covering events/edits/pulse overflow or insert-error swallowing.

findings.title: invoice.paid with no matching profile throws forever — a manually-created Stripe customer's invoice retry-loops through the webhook (round-1 nit, still open)
findings.evidence: `throw new Error(`Monthly allowance invoice ${invoice.id} has no matching profile`)` — the throw releases the event claim, Stripe redelivers on its full backoff schedule, and every delivery re-throws until Stripe abandons (~3 days of noise per invoice).
findings.why: Operator-created or migrated Stripe customers with no profiles row turn into multi-day webhook-failure noise that masks real failures in the dashboard; nothing is fulfillable, so the retries buy nothing.
findings.fix_shape: Ack unmatched non-subscription-linked invoices with a structured logError breadcrumb instead of throwing, or throw only when a customerId exists but the email fallback also matched nothing after a bounded retry count.
findings.deferral_checked: Recorded in the round-1 nit batch (register line ~1396, item 2); verified still present at HEAD — carried forward at low, matching the register.

findings.title: admin get_stats selects every profiles row unbounded — silently wrong stats past PostgREST's max-rows and a growing full-table read
findings.evidence: `const { data: profiles } = await adminClient.from('profiles').select('tier, role, credits');` then JS-side count/reduce over the returned rows — no .limit, no aggregate; PostgREST caps the response (default 1000 rows), after which total/premiumCount/totalCredits undercount without any error.
findings.why: The admin dashboard's headline numbers silently freeze at the row cap as the user base grows — a wrong-number bug that looks like a plateau, on the surface an operator trusts for business decisions.
findings.fix_shape: Replace with one SECURITY DEFINER admin_stats() RPC doing count(*)/sum(credits) grouped by tier/role — same pattern as the existing report_* functions this file already dispatches to.
findings.deferral_checked: Not in the round-1 register (admin-actions entries covered PII redaction and role gates), no in-file note; checked playbook §0.6 rulings — absent.

findings.title: create-checkout ignores the profiles read error from .single() — a profile-less authed user mints a fresh orphan Stripe customer on every checkout
findings.evidence: `const { data: profile } = await admin.from('profiles').select('stripe_customer_id').eq('id', user.id).single();` — .single() errors on zero rows, the error is never destructured, profile is undefined, so a new Stripe customer is created and the follow-up `.update(...).eq('id', user.id)` writes zero rows silently.
findings.why: Any user whose profiles row is missing (failed trigger, migration gap) accumulates one orphan Stripe customer per checkout and never gets a durable stripe_customer_id binding — the webhook's email-fallback then carries the whole matching burden for money events.
findings.fix_shape: Use .maybeSingle(), check the error, and upsert the profiles binding (or fail loud into the generic 400) — mirrors create-customer-portal's identity-match care on the same read.
findings.deferral_checked: No round-1 entry or in-file note; the sibling create-customer-portal read at line 72 already uses .maybeSingle(), confirming the intended idiom.

findings.title: Privilege-mutation RPC service_update_profile_metadata retains the default PUBLIC execute grant (no revoke-from-public)
findings.evidence: Statement-level census across all 134 migrations: the ONLY grant/revoke touching this function is `grant execute on function public.service_update_profile_metadata(uuid, uuid, jsonb, text) to service_role;` (017:366). No migration (incl. 062 'close_authz_gaps', which only drops a policy + enables RLS on 2 tables) ever REVOKEs the inherited PUBLIC grant. Its sibling service_set_credits got exactly this fix in 113.
findings.why: This RPC sets role/tier/is_founder — a privilege-escalation-shaped surface, and 062 GAP-2 explicitly designates it one of the trusted audited write paths after removing the direct profiles-UPDATE bypass. It retains the CREATE-time default PUBLIC execute, so it is callable by any anon/authenticated caller over PostgREST. Not a live hole: the body's first statement `perform public._assert_service_admin_actor(actor_user)` raises unless the JWT role is service_role AND the actor is developer/admin (fail-closed) — the same defense-in-depth gap 113 named for service_set_credits.
findings.fix_shape: A grant-only migration mirroring 113: REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.service_update_profile_metadata(uuid,uuid,jsonb,text) FROM public, anon, authenticated; then re-GRANT EXECUTE to service_role. Better: add a structural ratchet (like migrationSearchPathPin) asserting every SECURITY DEFINER money/privilege RPC is revoked from PUBLIC — the absence of such a guard is why this slipped when 113 fixed only one sibling.
findings.deferral_checked: Checked round-1 backend-3 (search_path, unrelated) and backend-1 (create-checkout rate limit); the 113 migration comment names service_adjust_credits + get_credit_balance as the locked siblings but NOT service_update_profile_metadata; no deferral ledger (playbook 0.0.2/0.6/0.8, DEAD_CODE_DISPOSITION) records this grant gap.

findings.title: search_path ratchet baseline can mask a LIVE pin regression when a baselined pre-094 function is recreated with a bare header
findings.evidence: The walker reads search_path from each function's net-current `create or replace` HEADER and is 'blind to ALTER' (its own comment, lines 28-31). 094 pinned the 74 pre-094 definers via an ALTER DO-block; their net-current headers stay bare `set search_path = public` (frozen in the 76-entry baseline). The 'adds no NEW' check only flags names absent from the baseline; the 'no stale' check only flags baselined names that became non-bare.
findings.why: A future migration that recreates any baselined pre-094 function (e.g. get_credit_balance/system_grant_credits) with the historical bare `set search_path = public` header resets its LIVE proconfig to bare public (create-or-replace overwrites proconfig; 094's DO-block never re-runs), reinstating the CVE-2018-1058 pg_temp-first posture — while the ratchet stays green (the name is still bare AND still baselined: neither 'added' nor 'stale'). The guard catches new bare definers and re-pins, but not regressions of already-baselined ones.
findings.fix_shape: Have the ratchet resolve the EFFECTIVE pin the way the DB will (treat a baselined function as pinned only if its net-current recreate is <=094 OR its header pins pg_temp), or add a rule that any migration recreating a baselined function must pin `public, pg_temp` in the new header (131's pattern). Low-risk class on Supabase per 094's own note, but the structural-prevention intent is currently defeatable.
findings.deferral_checked: Checked round-1 backend-3 (resolved by 131 + this ratchet) and the ratchet's own header comments — they acknowledge ALTER-blindness for the 103 service_* baseline entries but do NOT acknowledge the recreate-regression direction; no deferral ledger records it.

findings.evidence: No supabase/rollback/ directory exists; the down-migration convention is inline @rollback annotations present on only 22 of 134 files. New CREATE TABLE migrations have an implicit destructive down (`drop table`), and the hardening migrations have a 'roll back only to unblock a broken deploy, then re-apply' shape — leaving them unannotated makes the reversal path tribal knowledge exactly where a botched launch push would need it. findings.title: build-edge-shared.mjs imports esbuild as a phantom dependency — not in devDependencies, resolved via vite's transitive `esbuild ^0.27.0`, so edge-bundle regeneration floats with the toolchain
findings.evidence: `import { build } from 'esbuild';` — package.json declares no esbuild; package-lock shows only `node_modules/vite` depends on `esbuild ^0.27.0`. The freshness contract hashes INPUT SOURCES only (sourceHash), not the esbuild version, so two machines with different hoisted esbuilds emit different committed bundle bytes under the same green hash.
findings.why: A vite major bump (rolldown-era vite drops esbuild) or dedupe silently breaks `npm run build:edge-shared`; less visibly, regeneration is not byte-reproducible across installs, producing noise diffs in the committed supabase/functions/_shared bundles the Deno tests execute.
findings.fix_shape: Add esbuild (pinned) to devDependencies; optionally record the esbuild version in the .meta.json sidecar so a version-skew regeneration is visible in the diff.
findings.deferral_checked: Grep of round-1 register for esbuild: only unrelated mentions; not recorded.

subsystems.holistic:
This slice is the most hardened surface I have seen in a solo-built repo, and — unusually — its quality is load-bearing rather than decorative: in a project whose constitution is enforced by ratchets, the gate machinery IS the constitution. The round-1 highs in this slice were genuinely fixed, not papered over. VERIFY_DIST now has an unconditional hard-fail sentinel (vendorPdfLazy.test.js:407) so the first-paint budget can never again count green on a missing dist; check-domain-strict gained a broken-toolchain anti-vacuity sentinel that distinguishes "ran clean" from "did not run"; the Vercel ignoreCommand gate is a small masterpiece of fail-closed thinking — it inverts correctly around Vercel's exit-code convention, catches its own crashes (a thrown error would otherwise read as PROCEED), blocks token-less and metadata-less CLI prod deploys, dedupes re-run check names with success-wins logic, and layers a migration-currency gate on top, with every branch pinned by ciGateHardening.test.js and the REQUIRED_CHECKS list drift-guarded against ci.yml job names in both directions. The local/CI parity test, the e2e anti-vacuity guard (static discovery + runtime executed-count), the mutation sweep with its dirty-tree refusal, the five shrink-only baselines each verified to have an enforcing consumer, and the derived-not-curated chunk-split machinery in vite.config.js (engine-shared closure, eager module graph, icon and data splits — each with a documented fail-safe direction and a named enforcing test) together form a coherent anti-vacuity doctrine that the repo demonstrably applies to itself recursively: gates that verify gates, and a weekly sweep that plants regressions to prove the gates catch them.

The findings are correspondingly narrow, and the two that matter share one shape: the enforcement spine lagging an architecture move. The data-purity fence (lint rule + source-regex twin + mutation-sweep plant) still points at src/generators/rngContext.js, but the RNG seam moved to src/kernel/ — the one bug class the fence exists to stop is now importable around it, and the weekly sweep certifies the stale fence. Second, the stale-dist problem was fixed in the vacuity direction (verify:dist post-build) but not the false-red direction: check still executes the dist-reading contracts before build against the previous dist, a recurring operational tax the repo has already invented the cure for (the VERIFY_DIST skipIf idiom) and applied to exactly one assertion. Third, the soak surface has outgrown its CI lane: whole-world-soak is a real pass/fail watchdog — same-seed byte-identity at the composed-kernel level plus a cost envelope — that runs nowhere on a schedule, while the lane still runs only the religion-era probes under a now-stale "diagnostic-only" rationale.

As product surface, this slice mostly serves the operator, and it serves them well: error messages name the remediation command, the deploy gate's skip reasons explain the redeploy loop, and the generated artifacts (glossary, analytics dictionary, sitemap) are freshness-pinned so the user-facing references cannot drift from code. The audit soaks are simulation-substance instruments of real quality — deterministic, tuned-nothing, panel-structured evidence generators that read like lab notebooks. Residual weaknesses are honest and recorded: CSP remains Report-Only (adjudicated deferral), e2e runs against the dev server rather than the built bundle, e2e/ and api/ sit outside lint, and a handful of round-1 comment-drift nits persist untouched in the enforcement layer where comments are operator guidance. Grade A: the slice's core duties — single-point budget enforcement, fail-closed deploys, CI/local parity — are airtight; the deductions are two medium-grade fence-lag gaps and hygiene debt.
strengths: Fail-closed deploy gate done right: vercel-ignore-build.mjs handles the exit-code inversion, crash-as-proceed, token-less and CLI-metadata-less deploys, re-run dedup (success-wins + filter=latest), and migration-currency drift — every branch exercised by ciGateHardening.test.js against the real decideDeploy(), with REQUIRED_CHECKS ⇔ ci.yml job names pinned both directions and mirrored by the deploy job's needs list

A recursive anti-vacuity doctrine: VERIFY_DIST unconditional hard-fail sentinel, check-domain-strict's broken-toolchain sentinel, e2e static+runtime executed-count guards, ciCheckParity's bidirectional local/CI step parity, and a weekly mutation sweep that plants regressions to prove the spine holds — gates that verify gates

Derived-not-curated build splits in vite.config.js (engine-shared domain closure, chunk-level eager module graph, icon and data splits) where every rule documents its fail-safe direction and names its enforcing test; the budget itself is single-point (tests/build/vendorPdfLazy.test.js) and reached only through verify:dist post-build

Ratchet discipline is uniform and consumer-verified: all five scripts/.​*-baseline.json files have enforcing tests/plugins; baselines are shrink-only with explicit re-baseline commands and never-widen doctrine in every error message

Generated artifacts (sitemap, glossary, analytics dictionary, edge bundles) are all freshness-pinned byte-identical against fresh generation, with the edge-bundle sourceHash covering the full transitive input set via the esbuild metafile

The audit soaks are high-grade simulation instruments — deterministic, seeded, tune-nothing, panel-structured (whole-world-soak asserts composed-engine same-seed byte-identity, seed divergence, population bounds, and a serialized-bytes cost envelope with documented equilibrium findings)

CI job design shows real judgment: hostile-locale/TZ golden re-run (tr_TR + Chatham) as a required deploy gate, coverage floors run parallel off the critical path, slow jobs (mutation sweep, soaks) correctly quarantined to cron/dispatch with the `# deploy-gate: optional` marker convention the gate test understands

findings.title: layerBoundaries cycle baseline can silently miss a NEW cycle that threads through an already-finished node — enforcement depends on lexicographic DFS order
findings.evidence: `if (s === 1) cycles.add(canonical(stack.slice(stack.indexOf(next)))); else if (s === 0) dfs(next);` — a neighbor in state 2 (done) is ignored. Traced: with allowed cycle helpers>priorityHelpers, adding helpers→newMod→priorityHelpers is recorded ONLY if 'newMod' sorts before 'priorityHelpers'; otherwise priorityHelpers finishes first, newMod→priorityHelpers is a cross edge, and the new 3-cycle is never enumerated — gate stays green.
findings.why: This is the shrink-only architecture ratchet ('adding one → this fails'). The hole clusters exactly around the two ALLOWED cycles' members — helpers.js/priorityHelpers.js are hub generator modules where a new cycle is most likely to form — and whether it is caught depends on file naming, not structure.
findings.fix_shape: Replace back-edge enumeration with SCC comparison (Tarjan, ~30 lines): assert every strongly-connected component is a singleton OR exactly equals an allowed cycle's member set. SCCs are traversal-order-invariant, so the baseline becomes airtight instead of name-dependent. Also delete the dead `existsSync(base) ? null : null` at :112.

subsystems.holistic:
This test estate is the strongest artifact in the repository and, frankly, stronger than most professional codebases I have reviewed at any scale. Its defining property is that the guards guard the guards: the first-paint ratchet (vendorPdfLazy) carries not just a monotone byte budget but a full decision archaeology of every raise and reclaim, an unconditional VERIFY_DIST anti-vacuity test that cannot itself be vacated, and sentinel PRESENCE checks that prove the lazy-leaf ABSENCE checks are non-vacuous. The e2e layer has a forged-Playwright-JSON test of the script that detects all-skipped green runs. The enforcement-claims meta-pin makes prose like 'promoted to ERROR' gate-checked. ciCheckParity and ciGateHardening pin local↔CI parity and fail-closed deploy decisions by exercising real decision functions, not string presence. This is structural-prevention culture fully institutionalized.

Coverage shape against the new kernels is complete on the house pattern: every one of the ~7 new movers (upswing, resourceDynamics, convergence, momentum, settlement lifecycle, naval, peace-causal) ships a unit suite, a fenced pre-wire dormancy golden with a lit-path anti-vacuity twin, and manifest/walker registration checks. The realmCoverage walker deserves special mention — it source-scans worldPulse for forceable shapes and fail-closes the Counterpart Criterion with a shrink-only PARKED ledger at zero, which is the constitution turned into a test. Golden hygiene is verifiable in git: dormancy manifests were captured once, pre-wire, and never re-minted; the generator golden master's regens are all owner-signed commits. Round-1's top findings (VERIFY_DIST vacuity, stale-graph goldens, pglite skip-vacuity, self-minting manifests, catch-up persist round-trip, the everything-on composition gap, the pipeline flake) were all fixed with finding IDs cited in-file — remediation traceability most teams never achieve.

The weaknesses are real but peripheral. The e2e layer remains the thinnest stratum: 8 specs, two of which still contain the round-1-flagged assertion-free bodies, and no e2e touches the composer/docket/realm surfaces at all — the browser-level trust chain leans on the anti-vacuity ratchet plus jsdom smokes. Component-level coverage of the newest legibility surfaces (RealmDocket, RealmForecast, the WorldPulsePanel catch-up trigger) is module-eval-only while their store/domain layers are excellent — an inversion of risk, since the wiring seam is where these break. Two structural debts sit in the substrate: the dormancy oracle lives inside a test file imported by 21 suites (registration duplication plus rename fragility on the constitution's measuring stick), and the architecture cycle baseline's DFS enumeration is traversal-order-dependent, so a new cycle threading the existing helpers/priorityHelpers cycle can pass silently. Money-path coverage floors remain honest but thin (stripe.js floored at 0) — recorded round-1 and unchanged. Dormancy golden corpora are deliberately short-horizon (3 configs, 4–8 ticks); they prove no-write-on-load and short-run byte identity, while long-horizon drift is delegated to the soaks, which is a reasonable documented trade.

As product surface, the estate directly encodes the constitution: byte-identity, dormancy, the premium seam (28 security suites incl. pglite execution against real SQL), the ratchet, and the counterpart criterion each have named enforcement. Grade A rather than A+ because the browser-level layer and the newest UI seams lag the engine's rigor, and two substrate defects sit in constitutional gates themselves.

findings.title: upswingKernel freshSettlement reads the stale pre-clone updates array — same-tick cross-arc writes clobber each other and can re-arm a completed reconstruction
findings.evidence: `const freshSettlement = (id) => { const ui = updateIndex.get(String(id)); if (ui !== undefined) return updates[ui]?.settlement; ... }` — reads the ORIGINAL `updates` array, while all writes go to `nextUpdates` after ensureCloned(). The sibling settlementLifecycleKernel.js:471 correctly reads `nextUpdates[ui]?.settlement`.
findings.why: The B2 boom/bust pass (line 570, 594) and B3 flourishing pass (line 664, 677, 698) re-fetch via freshSettlement and then REPLACE nextUpdates[ui].settlement wholesale. If the same settlement was written by an earlier pass the same tick (recon condition mint, recon completion: reconstructedAt stamps + institution upgrade + history beat + skim), those writes are silently lost. Losing the reconstructedAt stamps lets recentUnreconstructedCalamity re-arm the SAME calamity within its 3-year window — a repeated legitimacy dividend/upgrade from one source, violating the kernel's own 'conservation absolute' header. Deterministic, but incoherent composition in a constitutional kernel.
findings.fix_shape: Change freshSettlement to read nextUpdates (the lifecycle-kernel idiom) — one-word fix; add a same-tick composition pin (recon-completes + boom-busts same tick; boom-mints + flourish-mints same tick) proving no write is lost. Consider extracting the shared freshSettlement/ensureCloned helper so the two kernels cannot diverge again.

dimensions.holistic:
This dimension is the constitution's home turf, and the codebase honors it with unusual rigor. The randomness architecture is genuinely fail-closed: rngContext throws in every environment when a draw happens outside a seeded scope, the sole escape hatch is a deliberately greppable named function, and the eslint fence bans Math.random, no-arg Date construction, Date.now, localeCompare, all toLocale* formatters, and Intl across src/generators, src/domain, and src/workers with per-tree explanatory messages — each backed by a source-regex guard test (domainWallClock, localeCompareGuard, localeFormatGuard) so skipping lint does not skip the law. The wall clock has exactly one sanctioned domain read (clock.js), and assertNowPinnedInTest converts the pin-now convention into a structural guard at both pulse entry points.

The loaded-dice law is not aspirational — it is implemented. The tick PRNG reseeds from `${rngSeed}::tick:N::interval`; the 70-site fork census across worldPulse shows stable keys nearly everywhere (per-candidate roll keys, order-symmetric battle keys sorted before joining, per-parent-per-tick satellite forks with draws consumed in codepoint order). Selection loops that precede a draw sort by codepoint with explicit tiebreaks; momentum's fold is deliberately permutation-independent; the frozen spatial digest builder documents and implements a provably deterministic Dijkstra with explicit heap tie-breaks, and no live mover writes into spatialDigest — everything mutable lives in spatialLedgers.

The dormancy audit of the five new kernels comes back clean at the gate level: upswingArcsEnabled, resourceDynamicsEnabled, settlementLifecycleEnabled, momentumEnabled, and interventionEnabled are all virtual (absent from DEFAULT_SIMULATION_RULES, preserved untouched through normalizeSimulationRules' input spread, fail-closed on garbage), all gates early-return with the same reference, ledgers drop-when-empty, and every kernel has a fenced dormancy golden in tests/property. The normalizer itself is a small masterclass: boolean keys coerce fail-closed, profile keys stay virtual until touched, and preset identity survives axis unlocks by design.

The blemish is inside the newest constitutional kernel. upswingKernel's freshSettlement closure reads the pre-clone updates array where its sibling lifecycle kernel correctly reads nextUpdates — so the kernel's three sequential arc passes (reconstruction, boom/bust, flourishing) can silently clobber one another's same-tick writes to the same settlement, and losing the reconstructedAt stamps can re-arm a completed rebuild, breaking the kernel's own conservation pledge. It is deterministic (same wrong bytes every run), so Law 1 survives, but it is exactly the composition-incoherence class this review hunts, it is untested (no same-tick composition pin), and it sits in the layer the endgame plans to light. The remaining findings are contract-legibility drift: a header advertising forks that do not exist, an escape hatch nothing adopted, cooldown stamps whose names overstate their semantics.

As product surface, determinism here is not just correctness plumbing — it is what makes the forecast (preview≡apply), the pause/dismiss equivalence invariant, and the catch-up collapse trustworthy, and those invariants are machine-enforced (residue-strip registry, byte-identity tests) rather than prose. Graded as mature production code for this ambition, the determinism constitution is the strongest subsystem I have reviewed in this codebase: one real high-severity composition bug in a dark-by-default kernel keeps it from a clean A.
strengths: Fail-closed rngContext: ambient draws THROW in every environment (test/dev/prod), with a single named, greppable escape hatch and a save/restore stack for nested generation — silent seed-divergence is structurally impossible in the fenced trees

The eslint determinism fence (Math.random / Date.now / new Date() / localeCompare / toLocale* / Intl banned in src/generators + src/domain + src/workers with per-rule teaching messages) is backed by source-regex guard tests so the law survives a skipped lint

Loaded-dice discipline is real: per-tick reseeded parent PRNG + 70 audited fork sites on stable keys (order-symmetric battle keys, per-candidate roll keys, per-parent satellite forks with fixed draw order), codepoint sorts before every selection loop, permutation-independent ledger folds (momentum)

Dormancy constitution fully honored by all five new kernels: virtual flags absent from DEFAULT_SIMULATION_RULES, same-reference early returns, drop-when-empty ledgers, and a fenced byte-identity dormancy golden per kernel (tests/property/*DormancyGolden)

The frozen spatial digest is a keystone done right: provably deterministic multi-source Dijkstra with explicit tie-breaks documented AND implemented, versioned re-canonize axes, and zero live-mover writes into the digest (census-verified)
wallClockNow is one seam with a structural test-time pin guard (assertNowPinnedInTest) at both pulse entry points; every domain timestamp threads caller-pinned now
normalizeSimulationRules fail-closes malformed booleans, keeps profile keys virtual-until-touched, and preserves unknown virtual flags untouched — the write-on-load class has no habitat

findings.evidence: Queue dispatch: `set(s => { if (s.settlement) { s.settlement.name = edit.payload?.newName; ... } }); if (renamed) get().persistActiveSaveEdit?.();` — persistActiveSaveEdit writes only {settlement, campaignState}. findings.fix_shape: Route the queue dispatch through renameSettlementImpl (one writer), add `name: trimmed` to its in-memory entry update AND its persistSaveUpdate partial; extend the §10.4 pin to assert persistedEntry(store).name and the cloud partial carries `name`.

findings.title: Deleting a saved settlement leaves campaign residue: settlementIds, mapState placements, and queued pendingEvents are never pruned

findings.why: A deleted member's id persists forever in campaign.settlementIds and placements (every reader is defensively filtered, so it is invisible), and its queued world-clock intentions survive until the next advance silently destroys them (see state-lifecycle-3). The campaign row also retains per-settlement worldState ledgers keyed by the dead id indefinitely.
findings.fix_shape: In the delete/bulk-delete flow (and destroySavedSettlement if desired), call removeFromCampaign for every campaign holding the id (it already handles queue pruning + persist); add a pin: delete a member save → campaign.settlementIds and pendingEvents no longer reference it.
findings.deferral_checked: Round-1 register grep 'settlementIds|dangling' — no entry; playbook §0.0.2 — no match; MASTER_MERGE_PLAN not applicable (same-lineage behavior).

findings.title: drainQueuedEvents silently destroys queued intentions whose member save is missing or inactive — violating its own §10 visible-refusal law

findings.fix_shape: Add a `missing_target` (or `target_inactive`) refusal branch before the continue so the entry rides the advance digest via queueRefusalNews like every other refusal; pin with a drained queue containing a non-member saveId.
findings.deferral_checked: Playbook §0.0.2 + W-COMPOSER-2 ledger row (§10 refusals 'refuse VISIBLY') — the law is recorded as shipped, no deferral for the missing-save class; round-1 register pendingEvents entries cover only the advance-in-flight clobber (since fixed with guards + pin).

findings.title: Persistence outbox mirror is not owner-scoped — cross-account boot replay prunes the prior user's parked writes as success
findings.evidence: `const MIRROR_KEY = 'sf_outbox_v1'` (global; contrast campaigns.js scopedLocalKey per owner). Boot replay (initOutbox, App.jsx:190) drains the mirror; outboxRunner treats a no-error supabase update as ok and prunes — a cross-user or signed-out update filtered to 0 rows by RLS returns no error.
findings.why: Sign-out → different sign-in on one device replays user A's parked ops under B's session: RLS matches 0 rows, PostgREST reports success, the op is pruned and its fingerprint recorded — A's pending edit intent is silently discarded and recorded as persisted. findings.title: hydrateFromSave adopts the PRIOR settlement under the NEW activeSaveId when the save carries no blob

dimensions.holistic: The state-lifecycle surface is in genuinely strong shape — visibly the product of a codebase that got bitten, wrote the bug class on the wall, and then built machinery against it. The owner's most-bitten pattern (a write that survives one path and ghosts another) has been systematically hunted: persistActiveSaveEdit gives every in-place content edit the same persist triple as applyEvent; resetSettlementIdentity is a real single-writer chokepoint that all four load paths route through (the round-1 setSettlement/generateSettlement leaks are closed exactly as the register prescribed); revertToSnapshot now re-derives systemState and folds it into the persisted campaignState; regenSection is canon-guarded and persists when a save is hydrated; and the M10b lastLivingAdvanceAt cursor is stamped inside BOTH Phase-2 commits (advance and resume) so the moved clock rides the same atomic persist — the phantom-re-catch-up hazard from memory is properly and thoughtfully closed, including the subtle resume case where the wholesale worldState re-derive would have reverted the stamp. The verified charge items all hold: COMMITTABLE_EDIT_KINDS exactly matches the commit dispatcher with fail-closed enqueue refusal and pins on both sides; the new wave ledgers (interventions, satellites, upswing, obligations, commitments, campaignPlans, navalTransit) all nest under the spatialLedgers conditional namespace, so ensureWorldState deep-clones and dormancy-gates them with zero per-ledger registration, and worldState now has an explicit ordered migration chain (v2 patron rename) modeled on settlementMigrations. The Track-K operation manifest (223-action denominator, fail-closed walker, shrink-only exempt ceiling) and the durable outbox (mirrored, supersede-deduped, per-key ordered, barrier-fenced, backoff-parked, status-chipped) are the kind of structural prevention that makes the next regression hard to write. Import surfaces (account file, gallery) share one scrub writer and fail closed with rollback. What remains is a thinner, edge-ward crop than round 1's. The one finding on a shipped, everyday surface is the town rename: the only live rename path updates the blob but never the save envelope's name — stale library card in-session and across reload, and a broken name-keyed neighbour-partner lookup — ironically sitting right beside the §10.4 fix and under a pin that asserts the blob half only. The second cluster is the delete-a-member-save path, which never mirrors removeFromCampaign's cleanup, feeding the drain's one silent-loss branch (missing/inactive save → continue with no refusal) that contradicts the same function's own §10 visible-refusal law. The rest are genuine low-grade residue: a dead-field pickler divergence, the still-open round-1 local-id coercion, an un-owner-scoped outbox mirror, and small undo/cap asymmetries. As product surface, the lifecycle work is unusually legible — refusals are typed and reach the digest, sync failures reach a banner and a retry chip, and the undo story (event scrub, pulse snapshot stack, version timeline) is coherent across paths. Graded as mature production code for this ambition: A−, held back from A only by the rename ghost and the delete-path residue being live-surface instances of the exact class the codebase has otherwise beaten.
strengths: resetSettlementIdentity is a true single-writer chokepoint for session-identity residue, routed from all four load paths (generate/hydrate/set/clear) — the round-1 F17/F19 leak class is structurally closed, not spot-patched

M10b lastLivingAdvanceAt is stamped inside BOTH Phase-2 commits (runAdvanceCampaignWorld and runResolveIntervalMajors) riding the same atomic persist, with the resume-side re-stamp correctly compensating for the cursor's pre-interval snapshot overwrite — the known phantom-time hazard is closed with its subtlest case handled

The spatialLedgers conditional-namespace design means every new wave ledger (interventions, satellites, upswing, commitments, obligations) inherits deep-clone-no-alias, dormancy byte-identity, and persistence for free — zero-registration extensibility that fixed the bug class before the waves landed

The durable outbox: localStorage-mirrored intent+payload, supersede-dedup per (saveId,kind), per-key ordering gates, members-before-snapshot barriers, backoff-with-park, Retry affordance, and a status chip — fire-and-forget cloud writes became a real crash-consistent pipeline

COMMITTABLE_EDIT_KINDS no-silent-drop contract enforced at the enqueue mouth with pins on both the domain and store sides; the Track-K operation manifest gives the whole mutating surface a fail-closed census walker

worldState now has an explicit ordered migration chain (WORLD_STATE_MIGRATIONS v2) modeled on settlementMigrations, whose own runner has forward-version detection, gap detection, and a chain-diagnostic test hook

Import lifecycle (account export/import, gallery settlement) is fail-closed, ownership-remapped, seed-scrubbed through one shared scrub writer, and rolls back partial batches — plus campaign tombstones + the pendingSync marker kill the deletion-resurrection cycle

Advance-in-flight + parked-pause sync-prefix guards are uniformly applied across every pulse mutator including the new docket ops (queue/cancel/update) and the regional slice — the round-1 lost-DM-intent window is closed with a dedicated pin

dimensions.holistic:
The security architecture that earned A+ in round 1 held its shape under fifteen waves of engine load — and that is the headline. The core disciplines are not just present but uniformly applied: every public projection is allowlist-constructed (PUBLIC_TOPLEVEL_KEYS fail-closed root gate; worldSnapshotPublic never spreads raw worldState), every client scrub has a pinned SQL twin with a drift test (toPublicSafe ↔ _gallery_sanitize_public_json field-for-field; COVERT_KEY_RE ⊆ the 089/127/128/130 snapshot scanner), every anonymous sink fails closed (rate limiters proceed only on a definite true; CORS never emits '*'; the owner-override email can never match empty; cron endpoints refuse outright when their shared secret is unset), and every token path compares in constant time — account-actions and verify-single-dossier hash-and-fold, auth-recovery goes further and floors the response latency so the reset-email send cannot become a timing oracle. The premium seam's constitutional half is provably intact: zero tier/auth/store reads anywhere in src/generators; tier gates reveal (BeliefDivergenceBand, RumorsTab, the PDF faith chapter), never generation. No secrets in the tree. The 132–134 analytics wave landed in perfect house style: SECURITY DEFINER, search_path pinned, service-role-only execute, id-free rollups, research-plane by inheritance.

Where the fifteen waves did leave a mark is exactly the class the round-2 synthesis predicted: census lag at the seams. The defense-in-depth hard-deny list — mirrored client-side (WORLD_SNAPSHOT_HARD_DENY) and server-side (the scanner's hard_deny array) and self-described as "must only ever GROW" — still names the original twelve worldState keys, while the waves added spatialLedgers (belief ground truth, foreign interventions, latent resource veins, covert ops), politicsLedgers (covert conspiracies), warPosture (covert flags), and religionStates. The allowlist construction keeps them out of real snapshots, and a raw-worldState smuggle still trips the original twelve, so there is no live leak — but the second wall did not grow with the house it defends. The same lag shows in the round-1 low that never entered a fix track: the import twin (stripImportConfidential) still omits config.latentPantheon while its display twin covers it. And the covert-text class remains exactly as recorded: the owner-gated impairment chip plus the registered war_mobilization lane — my sibling hunt (npc.corrupt vs the publicNpc allowlist, pulse writers vs currentTensions/conflicts, wizardNews gating, new-ledger display reads) found no third lane, which is genuine good news.

As product surface, the posture is honest: the CSP still ships Report-Only (recorded, owner punch list), which keeps DOMPurify as the sole XSS boundary on the one surface that renders user-authored HTML to anonymous readers — the highest-value residual to close, unchanged since round 1. The one fresh judgment call worth an owner glance is small: the PDF's live-world slice scrubs rumors and trade pressure to the player projection because "the PDF is shareable," yet feeds belief-divergence the DM projection on the same page, justified by the premium gate — money and audience are different axes, and the file currently conflates them. Overall: the strongest dimension in the codebase, one notch off perfect because the denylist-growth discipline demonstrably lagged the wave cadence and the round-1 lows are aging open.
strengths: Twin-pinning discipline: every client-side scrub (toPublicSafe, COVERT_KEY_RE, chronicle allowlist) has a server SQL mirror pinned by a dedicated drift/contract test (gallerySanitizeAllowlist.contract, snapshotDenylistDrift, gallerySanitize.pglite) — regressions on either side fail the gate

Uniform fail-closed posture: shared CORS allowlist never emits '*'; all rate limiters (ingest-events IP+actor, auth-recovery, log-client-error) proceed only on a definite true; cron endpoints (analytics-export, pricing-resync-cron) refuse when their secret is unset; OWNER_EMAIL override can never match empty
Constant-time comparison on every token path, including auth-recovery's constant response-latency floor so the reset-email send cannot leak answer correctness by timing

Constitution §3 (tier never touches generation) provably holds: zero auth/store/tier reads in src/generators; tier gates only reveal seams (includeCovert/includeGroundTruth convention consistently applied across 10+ read-models)

Analytics privacy architecture intact through the V2/A3 wave: peppered device hashes (null when pepper unset — fails safe), server-side consent clamp, recursive 64-char prose backstop, id-free rollups, service-role-only SECURITY DEFINER functions with pinned search_path

dimensions.holistic: This dimension is the round-1 success story: R1 graded it B with three HIGH structural findings, and the F5/F5b/catch-up-collapse waves fixed them the right way — with mechanism, measurement, and machine enforcement rather than spot patches. The frozen spatial digest is now shared by reference behind an idempotent deepFreeze with a correct Immer isDraft guard, which simultaneously killed the ~11×/tick 47-400KB clone and restored every distanceRead WeakMap memo to real once-per-advance semantics (20.3× measured, 2.67→0.13ms/tick, quoted in the commit). The M10b catch-up is genuinely one orchestrated interval now — one snapshot+drain, one Phase-2 commit, one persist, worker-eligible — and the lastLivingAdvanceAt cursor is stamped in BOTH commit paths (advance Phase-2 and the resume path), closing the phantom re-catch-up hazard the memory system flagged. The interval orchestrator's yield discipline is unusually correct (scheduler.yield preferred, MessageChannel macrotask fallback with an explicit note on why a microtask fallback never yields), and the worker client's failure taxonomy (sim-throw rejects, transport failure falls back once, per-tick watchdog, one-shot latch) is production-grade. The measurement gap is closed twice over: a committed tick-cost envelope gate (size ceilings, bounded-ledger asserts, growth-deceleration, machine-tolerant time trend) plus the whole-world soak parameterized to the 30-settlement envelope. Meanwhile the first-paint constitution didn't just hold through ~15 engine waves — it ratcheted DOWN nine times (1,255,985 → 1,121,903) while the waves landed, because the reclaim-then-thread discipline (find a data-table over-inclusion, excise it, fund the wave) actually works, and the VERIFY_DIST anti-vacuity guard keeps the gate honest. The new kernels are uniformly disciplined: virtual-flag early returns for dormant cost, drop-when-empty spatialLedgers, and prune-by-age or hard caps everywhere I looked (momentum MAX_LOOKBACK 260/RECEIPT_CAP 8, lifecycle SATELLITE_CAPS/HISTORY_CAP, statecraft mark decay, wizardNews 240, terminal impacts 250, pulseHistory 80, persisted missed rolls 48). What remains is residue, not structure. The R1 perf-scale-2 verdict prescribed a two-part fix and only part (a) shipped: ensureWorldState still deep-clones the whole mutable conditional-ledger set on each of ~10 snapshot rebuilds per tick, and the new waves roughly doubled the sub-ledger population riding that clone. The graph got exactly the right mechanism (a non-enumerable ENSURED_BRAND + ensureRegionalGraphOnce) but it was adopted at one call site — the hottest re-ensure sites still full-normalize every row ~10×/tick. And the forecast, which is the same 52-tick compute the advance moved off the main thread, runs in-thread. None of these is age-linear anymore (the gate would catch that); they are constant-factor waste that grows with wave count and realm size, all with existing, proven fix mechanisms. As product surface, the perf work reaches the eye where it matters: the catch-up has a busy state and a while-you-were-away digest, the advance has a determinate progress bar fed from the worker, and a 30-settlement year-advance no longer freezes the tab. Grade A- — the constitution's byte axis and the new cost axis are both machine-enforced, and the remaining findings are known-shape residuals of partially-adopted mechanisms rather than blind spots.
strengths: The catch-up collapse landed exactly per the R1 fix shape: runCatchUpCampaignWorld routes the whole ≤26-week span through ONE orchestrated interval (one snapshot/drain, one Phase-2 commit, one localStorage persist, one cloud sync), worker-eligible, with the M10b cursor stamped in BOTH commit paths (campaignAdvanceSession.js:299-313 and 495-512) — the recorded phantom re-catch-up hazard is structurally closed, and the living/autonomous split (pause-on-major vs auto-resolve) rides the existing pause machinery instead of new code.

Freeze+share of the spatial digest (worldState.js deepFreeze + FROZEN_CONDITIONAL_LEDGER_KEYS) with the F5b isDraft guard: kills the dominant per-tick clone, restores every WeakMap route memo (PORT_SET_MEMO/SEA_ADJ_MEMO/CANDIDATE_MEMO) to stable-identity hits, and converts a never-written convention into a throw-on-write guarantee — 20.3x measured and quoted in the commit.

The tick-cost envelope gate (tests/simulation/worldTickCostEnvelope.test.js) is a model cost gate: deterministic byte ceilings as the real assertion, growth-DECELERATION as the age-linear tripwire, and a machine-load-tolerant 10x time-trend bound instead of flaky absolute ms — plus the whole-world soak parameterized to --settlements 30 with per-year cost series.

First-paint constitution ratcheted DOWN nine times (1,255,985 → 1,121,903) across ~15 engine waves via reclaim-then-thread (npcData −51,957B, stressInstitutionEffects −21,664B, FP-G7 −3,260B funding the 14-verb composer lift), with the VERIFY_DIST anti-vacuity guard preventing green-on-nothing.

Uniform growth-bound discipline in every new-wave kernel sampled: virtual-flag early returns for dormant ticks, drop-when-empty spatialLedgers (dropSpatialLedger collapses the namespace), and caps/decay everywhere (momentum MAX_LOOKBACK_TICKS 260 + RECEIPT_CAP 8, lifecycle SATELLITE_CAPS + HISTORY_CAP 8, statecraft mark pruning, wizardNews 240, terminal impacts 250, pulseHistory ring 80, persisted missed rolls 48, settlementTickStates pruned to live ids).

The advance worker transport (advanceWorkerClient.js) distinguishes sim-throw (reject to atomic rollback) from transport failure (one in-thread fallback), with a per-tick liveness watchdog and a one-shot settle latch; the orchestrator's yieldToEventLoop correctly insists on a macrotask and documents why.

dimensions.holistic:
The question this dimension asks — do fifteen separately-built waves compose into ONE simulation? — gets a genuinely positive answer, verified seam by seam. The cross-wave couplings the designs promised are overwhelmingly real and traced in code: a calamity stamp (organic or DM-forced, through one shared resolver) arms reconstruction, which matures real ally-credit obligations from the generosity ledger and marks the stamp consumed so the cycle closes; a resource removal plants vein_exhausted, which the boom's bust flip consumes exactly as a severed artery (the W-DISCOVERY→W-UPSWING seam landed as designed); a live boom raises prospecting drive (upswing→discovery, the reverse direction) and a resource_strike is the mining-camp birth trigger in the lifecycle seeding drive (discovery→lifecycle); convergence's interventionAdjFor tilts the coup verdict; blockades sever supply through blockadeInterceptsSupply, feed economic_strangulation into the peace reasons, and deposit into commitment momentum; momentum's three consumption factors are wired into the strategy chooser, the belief reconcile, and the supply-web abandon floor; and the conquest motive reads the target's worth scaled down by the conqueror's own corruption leak — the extraction ceiling exactly as constitutionalized. The pulse kernel's mover ordering is explicitly reasoned in comments (calamity → generosity → intervention → upswing → lifecycle → treaties → war/peace reasons → momentum → cracks), each with its read-dependency stated. The counterpart criterion substantially holds: my sweep found 12 of 14 realm verbs live with organic twins, the two gray verbs honestly documented, and the settlement manifest covering resource/plague/corruption/generosity counterparts.

The defect mass sits exactly where the round-2 synthesis said it would — at seams — and my re-dispatch adds a specific sub-shape to that diagnosis: taxonomies wired at the exit but not the entry. The contest course kind exists in momentum's parser, its climb-down arm, and FORCE_RECONSIDERATION's wind-down, but no deposit source ever mints one, so interventions accrue no momentum and the LOUD_INTERVENTION constant guards an unreachable branch. The conscience door (counterEvidenceEffectiveness) is built and tested but the live discount is class-blind. The boom receipt's extraction/aid sources are hardcoded false. Each is a mechanism whose vocabulary outran its feeders — cheap fixes, but they are the difference between a taxonomy and a decoration.

The one law-level incoherence I found fresh is the blockade-blind peace read: the owner's "a blockade is the same as a siege" is honored by supply, peace reasons, and momentum, but upswing's peace01Of predates the navy and was never extended, so golden ages can mint under strangulation.

As product surface, the deepest structural fact remains: every one of these waves is dark. No preset or UI lights any of the nine gates, and the manifest's otherwise-excellent teaching refusals direct the DM to switches that do not render. Three gates have recorded owner-gated lighting; six have no ruling on file. Anti-stasis is therefore answered only architecturally: the up-traffic (reconstruction, booms, flourishing, discovery, steadings, generosity) is conserved, capped, cooled, and braked by construction, and its balance against the down-traffic is exactly what the everything-on checkpoint soak exists to measure — nothing I read suggests a snowball, and several pins (no-multiplier flourishing, absorption cap, cliff floors) exist precisely to prevent one. Grade A−: composition this deliberate across fifteen waves is rare; the entry-dead taxonomies and the unlit switchboard are what hold it from an A.
strengths: The one-cycle law is real end-to-end: organic and forced calamity run one shared resolver (resolveStrikeOnSettlement), stamp the same calamityHistory, arm the same reconstruction arc, and the completion marks stamps reconstructedAt so the trigger is consumed — no perpetual re-arming.

Cross-wave seams promised in the designs are consumed in both directions: vein_exhausted→bust and boom→prospecting-drive and resource_strike→mining-camp-birth form a genuine three-wave loop (upswing↔discovery↔lifecycle), each dormancy-safe by construction.

The counterpart criterion held under a full-denominator sweep: 12/14 realm verbs live through the sim's own kernel functions (force ≡ organic via shared resolvers, not assertion), the 2 gray verbs carry honest in-manifest deferral prose, and every live verb re-runs its gates at apply so a lapsed order refuses visibly rather than phantom-committing.

Momentum is wired into every major belief-consuming decision seam it named (strategy chooser via makeCommitmentLoad, belief reconcile via makeCommitmentDiscountFn, supply-web abandon floor) with byte-identity anchors (exactly ×1.0 uncommitted) at each injection point.

The extraction-ceiling constitution shipped: extractionUpswingAdj scales conquest EV by the conqueror's own corruption leak (foreignGripOf), bounded and 0-when-dark — greed priced by graft, exactly as ruled.

Mover ordering in pulseKernel is documented as load-bearing prose at every seam (why calamity precedes generosity precedes upswing precedes lifecycle; why momentum folds last), which is what made this cross-wave audit tractable at all.

dimensions.holistic:
The authored diegetic corpus is genuinely excellent — the best content writing I have seen in a generated-world product. newsVoice's eight crier categories, treatyDocument's compliance voice, causeLifecycleVocabulary's stage×cause floor, the lifecycle/momentum/convergence headlines ("A new steading rises near Thornwall", "climbs down from its war — with honour intact"), and the W-GUIDE-2 Surveyor's notes are register-consistent, settlement-agnostic, terminally punctuated, and mostly walker-pinned. The round-1 highs (CI-1 rumor token leak, CI-2 crier mis-route, CI-5 system-log card body) were fixed well, with in-code finding citations. Calamity-bucket neutrality holds everywhere I traced: type-blind crier cells, bucket-neutral ledger titles, flavor as DM suggestion/freetext only, "Force a calamity" label neutral. The concession/compromise vocabulary split is exactly maintained (settlementPolitics types 'concession' overt vs 'compromise' = corruption leash, covert:true). The premium seam on the flagship rumor surface fails closed and RumorsTab gates ground truth correctly.

The defect mass has migrated to exactly the pattern the Phase-A commit named: the display-vocabulary seams are guarded by HAND-LISTS, not registry-walked pins, so each new engine wave re-opens the round-1 wound. Five post-fix waves minted new impactKinds (generosity_*, boom, bust, blockade_declared, intervention_clash…) that (a) reach player rumor headlines as de-underscored engine compounds ("Merchants bring word of generosity relief in Thornwall", "…word of boom…") because WHAT_PHRASES and the strip-prefix list were never extended, and (b) re-trigger the CI-2 contradiction: boom/bust entries ride channelType 'trade_route', and newsVoice's channel fallback still fires for set-but-unclassified impactKinds, so a "Thornwall is booming" card carries a market-shortage crier quote — a polarity-inverted contradiction on the sim's showcase upswing beat. Both are regressions-in-class of FIXED round-1 findings; the CI-1 test pin exists but its KNOWN_WHAT list is a snapshot that no walker forces new kinds into. The same replication shows in the dead significance tiers: CI-6's nonexistent 'minor' (still unfixed, and absent from every F/G fix-wave list — a dropped confirmed finding) is now joined by generosityNews's 'minor' and upswingKernel's 'moderate'.

The guidance layer — this dimension's constitution — is half real machinery, half paper. The title= ratchet, register guards, dissociation checklist, and generated glossary (code-derived, freshness-pinned, honesty-gated) are real and admirable. But the registry's runtime semantics (one-whisper budget, unified sf:guidance:* dismissal, firsts gating, body copy via t()) are consulted by only 2 of 9 registered hosts; the W-COMPOSER-2 "mechanism whispers" (guidance.realmOrders/realmDocket) are dead copy rendered nowhere, WizardNextSteps still uses its own legacy dismissal key, and the walker asserts only that a host component FILE EXISTS. The criterion clause is currently satisfiable by inventory entry alone.

Smaller register warts: slug-tail deity display names mangle multi-word/custom deities on the paid PDF and public gallery; factionCompetition's generic headline stays ungrammatical ("X may government challenge"); post-CI-5 receipt reasons leak raw causeClass tokens and npc_N ids onto pill surfaces. Grade B+: superb content and held laws, pulled down by the unpinned seams that keep letting new waves regress the two flagship fiction surfaces.
strengths: Calamity-bucket neutrality holds end-to-end: type-blind crier cells (newsVoice calamity), bucket-neutral ledger titles with DM-only flavorSuggestion (calamityLedger), neutral 'Force a calamity' verb label — the engine never asserts a disaster kind.

The authored diegetic corpus is register-disciplined and walker-pinned: newsVoice 8 categories x 4 buckets with totality floors, treatyDocument compliance voice with honesty gate, causeLifecycleVocabulary stage x cause floor with the years-past constitutional pin, Surveyor's notes with second-person-required / UI-verb-banned register guard.

settlementRumors is a model premium seam: enumerated player whitelist, fail-closed deity-name scrub against activated public snapshots, fidelity internals never projected, DM truth block with divergence join — and RumorsTab gates includeGroundTruth on premium/elevated and never for playerView/public.

The concession-vs-compromise vocabulary split is exactly maintained (settlementPolitics BlocGlue: 'concession' = overt seats-for-majority; 'compromise' = corruption leash, covert:true), matching the owner's one-corruption-vocabulary ruling.

Real structural prevention where it was built: the title= shrink-only census (476 -> 471) actually catches cross-wave additions (it redded SM-3's tooltips), and the generated glossary is code-derived with a byte-identity freshness test and both-directions coverage pins.

Round-1 content-immersion fixes (CI-1/2/3/5) landed faithfully and are cited in-code; new-wave headline prose (lifecycle steadings, momentum climb-downs, convergence banners, resource strikes) keeps the house voice.

dimensions.holistic:
The DM workflow spine is genuinely mature, and visibly better than it was at round 1. The loop generate → canonize → advance → inspect → force → export now has real product craft at almost every joint: the pre-canonize Pulse tab teaches with an in-place "Start the World Clock" CTA (the round-1 two-canon-verbs confusion is resolved in copy); the advance path has a determinate progress bar, an auto-resolve toggle, typed refusal reasons mapped to honest GM-facing prose, a cloud-pending toast that refuses to claim success it didn't earn, and a real undo; the M10b catch-up now fires on campaign activation (round-1's top finding, fixed properly) and narrates itself through a transient while-you-were-away digest that surfaces its own failures instead of swallowing them. Inspection is deep — a seven-section inspector over pure read-models, a chronicle with per-tick causal diffs, a news feed with a house voice, and a persistent unreviewed-proposals badge that outlives the toast. The forcing surfaces honor the counterpart criterion's spirit: both composers gray-with-reason, refusals teach, and force applies through the world's own machinery. SessionMode, TableView, four PDF variants and a Foundry export make the at-the-table story concrete.

The defect mass sits exactly where the fleet's Phase-A synthesis predicted: the built-but-unwired seam between engine capability and DM eye. The one high finding is the sharpest instance in the whole workflow: the pause-for-majors mechanism — the product's central authority promise — has engine support for per-major verdicts but no surface that shows the batched majors or collects a decision; the only affordance resolves everything to defaults, silently, while the panel copy says "paused for your decisions." Around it cluster the same class at lower stakes: the docket's documented edit affordance that was never built, the forecast's candidate lane and realm beats (banked), the registered-but-unrendered whispers (banked), navy's design-promised legibility surface, pestilence's print-only read-model, and a tour that still teaches the pre-inspector UI. Secondary mass is error-honesty asymmetry: the Realm path maps every typed refusal to honest prose while the library's Advance Time swallows the same codes into a silent dead button — the two entry points disagree about whether the product explains itself.

What would a paying DM hit in the first hour? Mostly delight: the empty states invite, the locked anon Realm previews their own world's conflict band, and the first advance produces a legible pulse. The frictions they would hit are the false LAPSED alarms on peer-targeted trade routes, the multi-step manual navigation to edit a flagged docket entry, and — if they chose "pause for majors" — the discovery that resuming decided the war for them. None of these corrupt state; all of them erode the specific trust ("the world waits for your word, and everything explains itself") that the product sells.

Mechanism-vs-surface denominator: of 24 engine mechanism families, 17 reach a standing live surface, 26 of the worldPulse modules feed the news voice, and the remaining gaps are either banked (five read-model siblings, calamity ledger) or found here (navy state, pestilence live view, pause verdicts). The trajectory is strongly positive — both round-1 highs fixed, QuickInspector wired, RegionWakeReplay mounted, mobile gate built — and the remaining work is concentrated, well-shaped, and mostly byte-free lazy-surface wiring. A- as mature production for this ambition: the spine is excellent; the authority loop needs its last gate closed.
strengths: Catch-up-on-activation with an honest transient digest: busy state, weeks count, major beats from the same chronicle grounding, a capped note, and surfaced (never swallowed) failures — the round-1 high closed with real craft (WhileYouWereAway + runCatchUpCampaignWorld)

Error honesty on the Realm advance path: typed refusal codes mapped to plain GM prose (ADVANCE_ERROR_TEXT), a cloud-pending toast that refuses false success, and paused-state gating of proposal buttons with explanatory titles

Empty-state discipline: one CampaignEmptyState recipe reused across all inspector sections, and the pre-canonize Pulse tab teaches with an actionable in-place Start-the-World-Clock CTA instead of a dead end

Unavailability-teaches across both forcing surfaces: predicates wrap the sim's own gates, grayed-with-reason chips, refusal prose on stage and at the drain — the counterpart criterion is a lived UI convention, not a slogan

The inspect/explain loop is deep: 7-section Realm Inspector over pure read-models, chronicle scrollback with per-tick causal diffs from session undo snapshots, news in a house voice, dashboard change-channel deltas, and a persistent unreviewed-proposals badge
Premium seam as invitation: the anon/free Realm renders a blurred read-only preview of the user's OWN realm's conflict band rather than a wall — reachable, honest, funnel-correct
The at-the-table product story is real: SessionMode second-screen surface, TableView phone sheet, four phase-aware PDF variants (canon-only variants disabled with reasons), and Foundry VTT export
Self-gating dormancy carried into the UI everywhere: treaty tab, pantheon tab, realm strip, and living-world pips all render nothing on a dormant world — byte-identical surfaces, no false floors

dimensions.holistic:
This dimension is where the repo shows its most distinctive engineering culture, and mostly its best. The guard system is genuinely unusual in quality: every unification program (clamp, slugify, any-casts, raw buttons, forked colors) is enforced by an honest exact-set baseline that fails in BOTH directions — a new copy fails, and a migrated copy left in the baseline also fails, so wins are locked the moment they land. The any-cast ratchet even unit-tests its own detector against evasion fixtures (multi-line typedefs, prose "any", comment gutters). The story the baselines tell is real: domain-strict is at zero, any-debt burned 2291→2230 monotone, and all ~10 new wave kernels landed at zero any-holes, importing kernel clamp/slugify rather than hand-rolling. The feared copy-paste-kernel failure mode did not happen — the new movers share a real substrate (distanceRead's spatial-ledger seam, authorityFor, facetOf, foldObligations) and follow a legible convention (mover in worldPulse/, geometry/EV in spatial/). Barrel hygiene was fixed properly: region/index.js is curated with a first-paint law comment, worldPulse/index.js documents why it survives as a test-only API, and every store slice carries an explicit leaf-not-barrel note.

The defect mass sits in one place: the size-ratchet layer is the single guard built weak, exactly where growth is fastest. The F7 "domain max-lines 800" grandfather mechanism is literally `'max-lines': 'off'` — no ceiling at all for the seven listed files, no staleness lock, and no test equivalent of the exact-set idiom that governs every JSON baseline. In the two days since F7, pulseKernel grew 1092→1402 effective lines (+28%), applyWorldPulse 769→948 (crossing 800 and being added to the list — a documented 6→7 raise), warDeployment 1077→1124 — while stressors.js shrank to 477 and its override was never deleted, so that win is unlocked. Underneath, simulateCampaignWorldPulse is one function from line 204 to 2454; every wave splices another gated inline block into it. The kernels themselves are clean leaves — the accretion is confined to the orchestrator — but the orchestrator is the constitutional core (same-seed byte-identity lives or dies in its call order), and it is the least-guarded file in the tree. Phase A's holistic already endorses a composed lane registry post-merge; this slice's evidence says do it soon and re-arm the ratchet as per-file frozen ceilings in the same commit. Secondary gaps rhyme with the round-2 "guard-lag" class: store/pdf/lib have no size rule at all (settlementSlice 1298 eff, pdf viewModel 1041 eff), the component glob misses src-root App.jsx (766 eff), and the headless-spine walker is not transitive — six domain→lib edges (entities/text/customRegistry) are scanned by nothing, so one careless import into lib/entities.js would silently re-couple the engine to the client.

As product surface, this dimension's health is indirect but real: the reason fifteen engine waves could land in a week without the tree rotting is precisely the ratchet culture, and the reason the next regression will be a 3,000-line pulseKernel is precisely its one soft spot. Grade A−: the guard architecture is A+ work; the god-file trajectory and the off-switch grandfathers are a known, growing liability the current mechanism cannot even see.
strengths: The honest-ratchet system: exact-set, two-direction-failing baselines with monotone ceilings and self-testing detectors (domainAnyCastBaseline unit-pins its own counter against evasion fixtures) — wins are locked the commit they land.

All new wave kernels (upswing, resourceDynamics, settlementLifecycle, momentum, convergence, naval, peace, generosity) landed at zero any-holes, import kernel clamp/slugify, and share real substrate (spatial-ledger seam, authorityFor, facetOf) — no copy-paste-kernel drift; a consistent mover-in-worldPulse / geometry-in-spatial boundary convention.

Layer discipline holds and is enforced: zero React/Zustand/store imports across kernel/data/generators/domain (grep-verified), plus a self-contained deterministic cycle detector pinned to a 2-cycle shrink-only allowlist.

Barrel hygiene genuinely fixed: region/index.js curated to 39 explicit symbols with a first-paint law comment; worldPulse barrel documented as test-only API with zero production static importers (verified); store slices carry leaf-not-barrel import notes.

Dead code was adjudicated, not just found: DEAD_CODE_DISPOSITION.md is a model disposition ledger — per-file census with honest corrections to the review's own errors, owner-vetoable rulings, KEEP-AS-SEAM carve-outs, and baseline bookkeeping for every deletion.

dimensions.holistic:
This is the most honest test infrastructure I have reviewed at any scale, and the honesty is architectural, not aspirational: the gate audits itself. The round-1 test-dimension findings were not just fixed — they were fixed with the repo's own structural-prevention idiom, each closed hole leaving behind a named guard. The VERIFY_DIST green-on-nothing hole ([tests-1]) is now an UNCONDITIONAL it() that cannot be vacated the way the contracts it guards were; the pglite silent-skip class ([tests-3]) got unconditional existence describes in all 13 suites; the self-minting spatial goldens ([test-quality-3]) all now fail loudly on a missing manifest; the stale-regionalGraph golden bug ([tests-2]) was fixed AND pinned with a dedicated the-idiom-can-never-resurface test; the tsc-didn't-run vacuous pass ([build-tooling-docs-3]) got a global-diagnostic sentinel; the pipeline.property timeout flake got its 120s allowance. Layered on top: two-directional parity pins (npm-run-check ↔ ci.yml steps; REQUIRED_CHECKS ↔ job names with a tested opt-out-marker parser), a deploy gate exercised as executable decision logic including crash-must-skip, static AND runtime e2e executed-count guards, a hostile-locale/TZ determinism CI leg, a weekly mutation sweep that plants regressions and asserts the gate reds, exact-set ratchet baselines with both-direction freshness and in-test ceilings (strict errors pinned at literal zero; any-cast ceiling un-raisable even via --update), and dormancy goldens systematically paired with lit-path anti-vacuity so a typo'd flag cannot make a wave silently dormant forever. The realm coverage walker is a genuine fail-closed registration walker with a denominator anti-vacuity check and a shrink-only PARKED ledger — and its scan surface is actually complete (worldPulse has no subdirectories; no FORCE_ shapes exist outside it). Newest kernels (upswing, resourceDynamics, naval, lifecycle, momentum, convergence) all have dedicated kernel tests plus dormancy goldens.

The residue is small and mostly known. The one live gap in the stale-dist fix: the townMapLazy skipIf(!VERIFY_DIST) presence-gating idiom (the in-file "merge-integration lesson") was not propagated to vendorPdfLazy's three sentinel-PRESENCE tests or its byte-budget ratchet, so the pre-build test phase of a local `npm run check` (or any run after a lineage switch) still measures yesterday's dist and can spuriously red — the exact recorded gotcha, half-fixed. The property-test layer is the gate's only nondeterministic component (36 unseeded fc.assert calls); in a constitution built on same-seed determinism, an unreplayable heisenred is the flake class the repo's own docs say trains re-run habits. Known-open recorded items persist: the mutation sweep still omits the constitutional gates themselves (goldens/budget/dormancy — [tests-8]) even as nine new kernels raised the stakes; the 155-vs-187 comment and the beliefMap non-difference "differ" assertion ([test-quality-10]) remain. Grade A- as mature production code: the enforcement spine is exceptional; the deductions are the half-propagated freshness fix, the unseeded property layer, and recorded-but-still-open sweep coverage on the constitution's own gates.
strengths: Anti-vacuity as a culture: unconditional VERIFY_DIST hard-fail, e2e static+runtime executed-count guards, pglite migration-existence pins, walker denominator checks, and a tsc-actually-ran sentinel — every 'skip' path has a guard that makes skipping loud

Two-directional parity meta-gates: ciCheckParity pins npm-run-check ↔ ci.yml both ways; ciGateHardening pins REQUIRED_CHECKS ↔ job names both ways with the opt-out marker parser itself unit-tested on synthetic YAML

Deploy gating tested as executable decision logic (decideDeploy/runGate): fail-closed on missing token, API error, non-2xx, missing git metadata, migration-ledger drift, and crash-must-become-skip — not string-presence checks

Golden discipline: committed manifests, exact corpus-key match (no silent key adds/drops), explicit UPDATE_GOLDEN refresh, and dormancy goldens systematically paired with lit-path anti-vacuity so the flag gate is proven real

Ratchets with exact-set governance: both-direction freshness (slack below baseline also fails), in-test ceilings that --update cannot raise (strict errors pinned at 0; any-cast at 2252), per-file granularity
The hostile-locale/TZ CI leg (tr_TR + Pacific/Chatham) re-running the determinism suites — an executed end-to-end proof of the locale-leak class the lint bans guard at edit time
Round-1 test findings were closed structurally: each fix left a named regression pin (e.g. the stale-regionalGraph threading test, the VERIFY_DIST unconditional guard), not just a patch
